svg.text: NCALM: one harness, one protocol, N architectures
Everything that is not the architecture is held fixed. The only independent variable is the model class plugged into the same interface.
Held fixed (controlled variables)
• Data: The Pile (uncopyrighted), one tokenized stream
• Tokenizer: GPT-NeoX (Pythia), vocab 50,304, frozen
• Parameter budget: ~162M ± 0.5%
• Token budget per tier: 250M or 2.0B
• Effective batch: 65,536 tokens/step, seq 1,024
• Optimiser: AdamW (β2 0.99), wd 0.1, grad clip 1.0
• Schedule: linear warmup 1,500 → cosine to 10%
• Seed 42, AMP, same eval cadence (every 1,000 / 200 steps)
• Same GPU: one RTX 4080 SUPER (16 GB)
Known defects of the shipped eval protocol, fixed
in docs but not in the recorded runs: validation windows
are random (no fixed held-out set) and the val loader
inherits the training micro-batch, so GPT-2 was scored
on 2× the validation tokens per eval. Both favour the
challengers; gaps under ~15% are within eval noise.
ncalm.model interface
forward(tokens) → logits
trainer · data · profiles · telemetry
GPT-2 baseline (GPT-NeoX / Pythia-160M layout) · 162,322,944 params
12 layers, d 768, 12 heads, d_ff 3072, rotary 25%, parallel residual, untied embeddings
AENCA v7.1 · 161,994,241 params · 2.0B tokens
4 attention layers + an 8-call shared causal-conv/GLU loop (7.7% of non-embedding params)
AENCA v13 · 161,999,873 params · 250M tokens
4 transformer blocks whose Q and K are gated by a 625K-parameter conv "morphogen" field
AENCA v15 · 159,994,661 params · 250M tokens · no attention
2D reaction–diffusion NCA on a folded sequence · earlier variants v3–v12, v14 not all archived
Blue: the control. Orange: challengers.
Every run writes config.json, metrics.jsonl and analysis.json; the complete runs are in runs/.
